Use loopback (the default). Switch to VPN only if the target app rejects a localhost URL, which is rare in practice.

mTLS Bridge is a local mTLS proxy for Android. Point your app (Jellyfin, Nextcloud, Home Assistant…) to a localhost URL; mTLS Bridge intercepts the plaintext request, encrypts it with your client certificate and relays it to your self-hosted backend.
The private key stays in the Android Keystore (hardware TEE when available) and cannot be exported from the device.

Two modes are available. Loopback (recommended) is safer and uses less battery: each config has its own 127.0.0.1 port, strict per-UID isolation and on-demand startup. VPN is only useful for apps that reject a localhost URL.

Android 17 blocks loopback (127.0.0.1) traffic between profiles: the target app must be in the same profile as mTLS Bridge. An app in the work profile or in the Private space cannot reach a proxy in the main profile. Install mTLS Bridge in that profile as well and create the config there.

If your server is on the local network (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x, 100.64.x.x…), Android 17 asks for the \"Nearby devices\" permission (local network access) before starting the proxy. Without it, connections to that server fail.
If your administrator sent you an mtls-bridge-bundle .zip file:

1. Open the menu (three dots) at the top of the list → Import
2. Select the .zip
3. Enter the passphrase (sent separately by your administrator)
4. All configs appear, already active
5. Open your app (e.g. Jellyfin) and enter the URL shown on the config card
Optional: check \"%1$s\" so the bundle is not left lying around on your file system.
To roll out mTLS Bridge to employees without them touching openssl: this bash script generates a .zip ready to import. The employee only has to tap it.
Adjust the variables at the top of the script (config_id, host, CA…). The random passphrase is printed at the end: send it to the employee over a separate channel (Signal, Matrix, SMS).
• Private key: in the Android Keystore (TEE / StrongBox), cannot be exported from the device. The UI shows the level actually obtained (StrongBox / TEE / Software).
• Configs: stored encrypted (SQLCipher AES-256-GCM, passphrase wrapped by an AES Keystore master key).
• Isolation: each loopback proxy has its own fail-closed UID check through ConnectivityManager.getConnectionOwnerUid, so no other app can intercept the session.
• Audit: all events (bind, accept, reject, bridge…) are stored in the encrypted database and can be viewed per config. Automatically purged after 7 days.
